Ajay Jadeja

Tests 1992–2000  ·  Born 1 February 1971  ·  Bats right-handed  ·  Bowls right-arm medium

A stylish, quick-witted batter and brilliant fielder from Jamnagar's cricketing royal family, who later helped steer Afghanistan to a memorable World Cup.

Where it began

Ajay Jadeja was born in Jamnagar on 1 February 1971, into the old royal family of Nawanagar, a family steeped in the game. Among his relatives were K. S. Ranjitsinhji and K. S. Duleepsinhji, the two cricketers after whom India's Ranji Trophy and Duleep Trophy are named.

He went to school in Delhi and Rajkot, and then on to Hindu College in Delhi. Cricket was never going to be far away.

The player

He played 15 Tests between 1992 and 2000, making 576 runs at 26.18 with four fifties and a best of 96. It was in the one-day game, though, that he truly shone: he played 196 one-day internationals, was vice-captain for a long spell and led India 13 times. He was part of the side that won the 1995 Asia Cup.

His most famous innings came in Bangalore, in the 1996 World Cup quarter-final against Pakistan. He made 45 from 25 balls, taking 40 runs off the last two overs from Waqar Younis. In Sharjah he once won a match against England by taking 3 wickets for 3 runs in a single over.

What made him special

He learned a great deal from Kapil Dev, and he brought style, a sharp cricket brain and real athleticism to the side. He read pitches and the state of a match well, ran hard between the wickets and had a flair that the crowds loved. He was one of the first Indian fielders to stand out on the world stage, and he began as he meant to go on, diving forward on debut to catch Allan Border.

Test cricket never quite gave him what the one-day game did. That 96 was as close as he came to a Test hundred.

Away from the middle

After his playing days he became a coach and a busy commentator and pundit, in English, Hindi and Gujarati. In 2023 he was Afghanistan's mentor at the World Cup, where they won four matches, England and Pakistan among them, and their players and coach thanked him warmly for it.

And finally

He also acted alongside Sunny Deol in the 2003 film Khel, danced on the first series of Jhalak Dikhhla Jaa, and in October 2024 was named heir to the Jam Saheb of Nawanagar. Not many international cricketers can list a film, a dance show and a royal title among their achievements off the field.
